notes: Each fixture needs its own real bytes/sha256 measured against the actual object in MinIO -- never a single shared size for every file, and never a part count inferred from bytes (structural splitting + re-encoding can change the effective size).

size_class is derived from the ACTUAL byte count vs size_threshold_bytes (16 MiB, the SplitFile threshold in internal/usecase/splitfile.go): 'small' means the original URL is returned unsplit; 'large' means the Splitter fans it out into parts.

All 13 fixtures below are `verified: true`: every bytes/sha256 value was freshly re-fetched and re-hashed against the live MinIO 'dataset' bucket (deploy/docker-compose.test.yaml, localhost:19000) via `go run ./loadtest/tools/verifyfixtures -write` on verified_at. The six small PDF/DOCX/XLSX fixtures and both boundary CSVs were generated by tmp/generate_real_fixtures.py (randomized real sentences/rows, not padding) and uploaded via `go run ./loadtest/tools/seedfixtures`; re-run both if the underlying MinIO data is ever reset.

If a future entry is added as a placeholder (object not uploaded yet), mark it `verified: false` with null bytes/sha256 -- k6/load_test.js refuses unverified fixtures by default (ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_FIXTURES=false) specifically so a capacity run never silently rests on unconfirmed data.

expected_parts is 1 for every size_class=small fixture: that is a direct contract guarantee (SplitFile returns the original URL as the sole part whenever the real file is <= size_threshold_bytes), not an inference about how a large file would be cut.

expected_parts is left null for every size_class=large fixture until it has actually been observed: publish that single fixture once, read the resulting SUCCESS event on stream:doc-extractor:output, and copy its `total` field here. Do not compute it from ceil(bytes / 16MiB).

url is the MinIO address reachable from INSIDE the docker-compose network (what gets embedded in the input event's file_path, since the Splitter/Extractor containers fetch it, not the k6 host). url_host is the same object reachable from the host (e.g. via deploy/docker-compose.test.yaml's published MinIO port), for the verifyfixtures tool and for manual smoke checks.

Two formats flagged 'synthetic padding' below (see docs/load-test-review-event-sourcing.md P2) are generated with comment-padding (PDF) or ZIP_STORED, uncompressed, low-structure content (DOCX/XLSX): their physical byte count is real, but they may not represent the CPU/memory cost of extracting an equivalent real-world document. Treat them as one data point, not a stand-in for all real documents of that size.
